DAMGHANI:v1p218/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p218/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p218/r5.claim: Zakāt can mean charity given by the parents.

BURSEVI:v5p245#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p245#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p245#2/r1.claim: حنانا is joined to الحكم, with its indefinite form magnifying it; the word moves from longing to compassion and mercy, either God's great mercy for John or mercy placed in his heart for others.
BURSEVI:v5p245#2/r1.anchor: {وحنانا من لدنا} عطف على الحكم وتنوينه للتفخيم

BURSEVI:v5p245#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p245#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p245#2/r2.claim: Zakat can mean purity from sin, charity God gave to his parents, or that God enabled John to give charity.

BURSEVI:v5p245#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p245#2/r3.speaker: الإمام
BURSEVI:v5p245#2/r3.claim: The Imam says compassion did not lead John to neglect an obligation; God joined kindness with freedom from failures in duty, as 24:2 warns against misplaced pity.
BURSEVI:v5p245#2/r3.anchor: لم تدعه شفقته إلى الإخلال بواجب لأن الرأفة ربما أورثت ترك الواجب

BURSEVI:v5p245#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p245#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p245#2/r4.claim: John was obedient and avoided sins; he neither committed a sin nor even intended one.
BURSEVI:v5p245#2/r4.anchor: {وكان تقيا} مطيعا متجنبا عن المعاصي لم يعمل خطيئة ولم يهم بها قط

BURSEVI:v5p246/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p246/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p246/r3.claim: The living heart receives the book of divine effusion by God's power rather than weak human power and becomes knowing, wise, merciful, pure of attachment to other-than-God, and pious.
BURSEVI:v5p246/r3.anchor: يا يحيى خذ كتاب الفيض الإلهي بقوة ربانية لا بقوة إنسانية لأنه خلق الإنسان ضعيفا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r1.claim: Ḥanānan coordinates with judgment and amplifies the gift; its root connotes longing and affection, then mercy and compassion.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r1.anchor: عطف على ( الحكم ) وتنويه للتفخيم وهو في الأصل من حن إذا ارتاح واشتاق

ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r2.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والضحاك وعكرمة والفراء وأبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r2.claim: These authorities, along with one report from Ibn Abbas, interpret ḥanān as mercy; cited poetry confirms the usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r2.anchor: وإلى تفسيره بالرحمة هنا ذهب الحسن وقتادة والضحاك وعكرمة والفراء وأبو عبيدة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r3.claim: Min ladunnā attaches to an omitted adjective, marking John's immense mercy as both inherently great and specially bestowed by God.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r3.anchor: والجار والمجرور متعلق بمحذوف وقع صفة مؤكدة لما أفاده التنوين من الفخامة الذاتية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r4.claim: A report from Mujahid gives the same meaning: God granted John great mercy from His own presence.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r5.claim: Another explanation is compassion in John's heart for his parents and others; its divine source marks it as approved or unusually abundant.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : المراد وآتيناه رحمة في قلبه وشفقتة على أبويه وغيرهما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد وعكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r6.claim: They explain ḥanān as love: God made John beloved by people, comparable to the love bestowed in 20:39.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p72#2/r6.anchor: وعن ابن زيد أن الحنان هنا المحبة وهو رواية عن عكرمة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p73/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report cited by Ibn Abi Hatim, interprets zakāt as blessing; John was made beneficial and a teacher of goodness.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73/r1.anchor: وزكاة ( أي بركة كما أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v16p73/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73/r2.claim: Other readings take zakāt as charitable giving: alms to people, charity toward his parents, or charity granted through him; al-Zajjaj says it means purity from sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73/r2.anchor: وقيل : الزكاة الصدقة والمراد ما يتصدق به والعطف على حاله آتيناه ما يتصدق به

ALUSI-FULL:v16p73/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73/r3.claim: Taqiyyan means obedient and avoiding sins; reports say John neither committed nor intended a sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73/r3.anchor: مطيعا متجنبا عن المعاصي وقد جاء في غير ما حديث أنه عليه السلام ما عمل معصية ولا هم بها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p73/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73/r4.claim: Mujahid reports that John's food was grass and that fear of God made him weep so intensely his tears grooved his face and could pierce tar on his eye.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73/r4.anchor: وأخرج مالك وأحمد في الزهد وابن المبارك وأبو نعيم عن مجاهد قال : كان طعام يحيى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p73/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73/r5.claim: The word ḥanān may also be parsed as a verbal noun, a causal object, or coordinated with ṣabiyyan, depending on its sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73/r5.anchor: وجوز أن يجعل مفعولا لأجله وأن يجعل عطفا على ( صبيا )

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p221/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p221/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p221/r11.claim: Ḥanān means mercy from God; a line by al-Ḥuṭayʾah uses taḥannun to mean showing mercy.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p221/r11.anchor: {وحنانا من لدنا} رحمة من عندنا، قال الحطيئة لعمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه: تحنن علي هداك المليك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: يعني بالزكاة الطاعة والإخلاص.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222/r2.speaker: قتادة والضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222/r2.claim: Zakāh means righteous action; al-Ḍaḥḥāk agrees with Qatādah.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة رضي الله عنه: هي العمل الصالح، وهو قول الضحاك.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222/r3.claim: The verse means God granted mercy and tenderness toward people so Yaḥyā would call them to obey their Lord and do righteous deeds sincerely.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222/r3.anchor: ومعنى الآية: وآتيناه رحمة من عندنا وتحننا على العباد، ليدعوهم إلى طاعة ربهم ويعمل عملا صالحا في إخلاص.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222/r4.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222/r4.claim: Zakāh is a charitable gift God bestowed on Yaḥyā's parents.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: يعني صدقة تصدق الله بها على أبويه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222/r5.claim: Taqiy means Muslim, sincere, and obedient; in his piety Yaḥyā never committed a sin or intended one.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222/r5.anchor: {وكان تقيا} مسلما ومخلصا مطيعا، وكان من تقواه أنه لم يعمل خطيئة ولا هم بها (1)

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:13-15/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:13-15/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:13-15/r1.claim: Divine ḥanān is mercy toward Yahya or tenderness in his heart toward his parents and others; zakāh is purity from sins, God's charitable gift to his parents, or his being enabled to affirm people. He was obedient and avoided sin.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:13-15/r1.anchor: رحمة منا عليه أو رحمة وتعطفا في قلبه على أبوييه وغيرهما

BIQAI-FULL:v4p523/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p523/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p523/r14.claim: God grants Yahya tenderness, reverence, gentleness of heart, provision, and blessing directly from Himself, without teaching or experience.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p523/r14.anchor: { حنانا } أي رحمة وهيبة ووقارا ورقة قلب ورزقا وبركة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p523/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p523/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p523/r15.claim: His zakāh is purity of intention that flows into his words and actions; piety is his natural disposition.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p523/r15.anchor: { وزكاة } أي طهارة في نيته تفيض على أفعاله وأقواله { وكان } أي جبلة وطبعا { تقيا }

DURR-FULL:v5p485/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r2.claim: Ikrima reports Ibn Abbas tentatively understands “hanan” as God's tenderness and mercy toward creation.
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r2.anchor: من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وحنانا} قال: لا أدري ما هو إلا أني أظنه تعطف الله

DURR-FULL:v5p485/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r3.claim: When Sa'id ibn Jubayr asked Ibn Abbas about “hanan,” he gave no explanation.
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: سألت ابن عباس عن قوله: {وحنانا} فلم يجر فيها شيئا

DURR-FULL:v5p485/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “hanan from Us” as mercy from God.
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وحنانا من لدنا} قال: رحمة من عندنا

DURR-FULL:v5p485/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas confirms Arabs use “hanan” for mercy and cites Tarafa's line.
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن نافع بن الأزرق قال له أخبرني عن قوله: {وحنانا من لدنا} قال: رحمة من عندنا

DURR-FULL:v5p485/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r6.claim: Mujahid explains “hanan” as tenderness from Yahya's Lord.
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد {وحنانا من لدنا} قال: تعطفا من ربه عليه

DURR-FULL:v5p485/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r7.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r7.anchor: عن الحسن {وحنانا من لدنا} قال: الرحمة

DURR-FULL:v5p485/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r8.speaker: الربيع
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r8.claim: Al-Rabi says it is mercy from God, whose gift nobody else controls.
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r8.anchor: عن الربيع {وحنانا من لدنا} قال: {رحمة من عندنا} لا يملك عطاءها أحد غيرنا

DURR-FULL:v5p485/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r9.speaker: سعيد الجهني
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r9.claim: Sa'id al-Juhani interprets “hanan” as loving affection.
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r9.anchor: عن سعيد الجهني في قوله: {وحنانا من لدنا} قال: الحنان المحبب

DURR-FULL:v5p485/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r10.claim: Qatada says “hanan” is mercy and “zakat” means charity.
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r10.anchor: عن قتادة {وحنانا من لدنا} قال: رحمة من عندنا {وزكاة} قال صدقة

DURR-FULL:v5p485/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets “zakat” as blessing and says Yahya was pure and did not sin.
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وزكاة} قال: بركة وفي قوله: {وكان تقيا} قال: طهر

DURR-FULL:v5p485/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r12.speaker: ابن عيينة
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r12.claim: Ibn Uyayna says Yahya neither disobeyed God nor entertained disobedience.
DURR-FULL:v5p485/r12.anchor: عن سفيان بن عيينة أنه سئل عن قوله: {وكان تقيا} قال: لم يعصه ولم يهم بها

QUSHAYRI:v2p237/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p237/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p237/r6.claim: God-given compassion and purity include purification and enabling for both acquired piety and piety bestowed directly by divine grace.
QUSHAYRI:v2p237/r6.anchor: فإن التقوى على قسمين : مجموع ومجلوب يتوصل إليه العبد بتكلفه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p76/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p76/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p76/r1.claim: حنان means compassion; it is also an attribute of God, and the expression حنانيك means compassion upon compassion, showing Yahya's divinely bestowed quality exceeds ordinary human measure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p76/r1.anchor: والحنان : الشفقة . ومن صفات الله تعالى الحنان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p76/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p76/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p76/r2.claim: زكاة means purification of the soul from evil, as in the command to purify oneself, or it may mean blessing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p76/r2.anchor: والزكاة : زكاة النفس ونقاؤها من الخبائث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p76/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p76/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p76/r3.claim: تقي is an intensive form meaning devoted to avoiding what conflicts with religion; كان تقيا indicates this quality was firmly established.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p76/r3.anchor: وجيء في وصفه بالتقوى بفعل { كان تقيا } للدلالة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r7.claim: Hananan is coordinated with judgment and zakatan with it, so “We gave” governs all three; alternatively hananan can attach to “as a child.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r7.anchor: وحنانا عطف على قوله الحكم وزكاة عطف عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r8.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r8.claim: Most commentators gloss hanan as mercy, tenderness, and love; ʿAta instead interprets it as exaltation from God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r8.anchor: والحنان الرحمة والشفقة والمحبة قاله جمهور المفسرين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r9.claim: Hanan and hananayn may be two forms with the same meaning or a singular and its dual; Arabic also uses hanan for sacred matters belonging to God.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r10.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r10.claim: ʿAta b. Abi Rabah interprets hananan min ladunna as exaltation from God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r10.anchor: وقال عطاء بن أبي رباح حنانا من لدنا بمعنى تعظيما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas said he did not know the meaning of hanan.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r12.claim: Zakah means purification and growth in good works; taqiy means devotional.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r12.anchor: التطهير والتنمية في وجوه الخير والبر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r13.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r13.claim: A report through ʿAbd Allah b. ʿAmr says every child of Adam comes on Judgment Day with sin except Yahya b. Zakariya.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r13.anchor: من طريق عبد الله بن عمرو عن النبي عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r14.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r14.claim: Qatada says Yahya never disobeyed God in minor or major matters and never desired a woman.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r14.anchor: إن يحيى عليه السلام لم يعص الله قط بصغيرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r15.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r15.claim: Mujahid says Yahya ate grass and that tears wore permanent channels in his cheeks.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p7#2/r15.anchor: كان طعام يحيى العشب وكان للدمع في خده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8/r1.claim: Poetic evidence for hanan comes from al-Nabigha and al-Mundhir b. Ibrahim al-Kalbi.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r1.claim: The syntax means God also gave Yaḥya tenderness.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r2.claim: The phrase can mean that God made Yaḥya a source of compassion for his contemporaries.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r3.speaker: ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r3.claim: The first of six interpretations of ḥanān is mercy, also held by a number of early exegetes and grammarians.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r3.anchor: أحدها أنه الرحمة رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r4.claim: A cited line asks for mercy, and the dual expression ḥanānik appears in a verse by Ṭarafa; Ibn Qutayba traces the word to a she-camel's care for its young.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r4.anchor: تحنن علي هداك المليك فإن لكل مقام مقالا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r5.claim: He says linguists agree ḥanān means mercy, and God did this out of mercy for Yaḥya's parents and to purify him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r5.anchor: لم يختلف اللغويون أن الحنان الرحمة والمعنى فعلنا ذلك رحمة لأبويه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r6.claim: A second view defines ḥanān as God's tenderness toward Yaḥya.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r6.anchor: والثاني أنه التعطف من ربه عليه قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r7.claim: He defines ḥanān as gentleness; another report from him gives blessing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r7.anchor: والثالث أنه اللين قاله سعيد بن جبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r8.speaker: عكرمة وابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r8.anchor: والخامس المحبة قاله عكرمة وابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r9.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r9.claim: He defines ḥanān as exaltation or reverence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r9.anchor: والسادس التعظيم قاله عطاء بن أبي رباح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r10.speaker: الضحاك وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r10.claim: The first of four interpretations of zakāh is righteous action.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r10.anchor: أحدها أنها العمل الصالح قاله الضحاك وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r11.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r11.claim: Zakāh can mean charity: God made Yaḥya a gift given in charity to his parents.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r11.anchor: أن معنى الزكاة الصدقة فالتقدير إن الله تعالى جعله صدقة تصدق بها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r12.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r12.claim: Another interpretation takes zakāh to mean purification.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r12.anchor: والثالث أن الزكاة التطهير قاله الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r13.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r13.claim: He takes zakāh to mean an increase in goodness beyond what was already described.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r13.anchor: والرابع أن الزكاة الزيادة فالمعنى وآتيناه زيادة في الخير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r14.claim: God made Yaḥya fear Him and associate no one with Him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r14.anchor: جعلته يتقيني لا يعدل بي غيري

SULAMI:v1p423#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p423#2/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p423#2/r1.claim: The gift of tenderness from God brought Yahya expansiveness and familiar intimacy.
SULAMI:v1p423#2/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : ذلك الذي أوجب له الانبساط والدلال

SULAMI:v1p423#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p423#2/r2.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p423#2/r2.claim: Yahya received divine mercy and purification from people's suspicions, and his piety consisted in turning from everything besides God and facing Him.
SULAMI:v1p423#2/r2.anchor: وقال سهل : رحمة من عندنا وطهرة طهرناه بها من ظنون الخلق فيه وكان تقيا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains hannan as mercy from God; Ikrima, Qatada, and al-Dahhak agree, with al-Dahhak adding that none besides God can grant it and Qatada that Zakariya received this mercy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {وحنانا من لدنا} يقول: ورحمة من عندنا، وكذا قال عكرمة، وقتادة، والضحاك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r2.claim: Mujahid interprets hannan as tender affection from the Lord toward Yahya.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {وحنانا من لدنا} وتعطفا من ربه عليه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r3.claim: Ikrima also glosses hannan as love upon Yahya.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r3.anchor: وقال عكرمة: {وحنانا من لدنا} [قال: محبة عليه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says hannan means love.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: أما الحنان فالمحبة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r5.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r5.claim: Ata ibn Abi Rabah interprets the phrase as grandeur from God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r5.anchor: وقال عطاء بن أبي رباح: {وحنانا من لدنا} ] (4) ، قال: تعظيما من لدنا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says he did not know the meaning of hannan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لا والله ما أدري (1) ما حنانا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r7.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says that when he asked Ibn Abbas about hannan, Ibn Abbas had no answer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r7.anchor: فقال: سألت عنها عباس، فلم يحر (2) فيها شيئا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r8.claim: The syntax joins hannan to the gift of wisdom; God gave wisdom and affection and made Yahya pure; hannan is loving compassion like a camel's tenderness for its young.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r8.anchor: فالحنان هو المحبة في شفقة وميل كما تقول العرب: حنت الناقة على ولدها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r9.speaker: شاعر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r9.claim: An unnamed poet's line uses tender solicitude, illustrating hannan as affectionate compassion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r9.anchor: تحنن (5) علي هداك المليك … فإن لكل مقام مقالا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r10.claim: A report from Anas says a man remains in Hell calling for a thousand years, O Hannan, O Mannan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r10.anchor: عن أنس، رضي الله عنه، أن (6) رسول الله صلى الله عليه قال: "يبقى رجل في النار ينادي ألف سنة:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r11.speaker: طرفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r11.claim: Tarafa's line uses ḥanānik as a fixed expression; Ibn Kathir notes some treat the form as its own dialect.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r11.anchor: كما قال طرفة: أنا منذر أفنيت فاستبق بعضنا … حنانيك بعض الشر أهون من بعض

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p217/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p217/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p217/r1.claim: Zakah is coordinated with hannan and means purification from impurity, sins, and transgressions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p217/r1.anchor: فالزكاة الطهارة من الدنس والآثام والذنوب.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p217/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p217/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p217/r2.claim: Qatada interprets zakah as righteous action; al-Dahhak and Ibn Jurayj call it pure righteous action, and Ibn Abbas calls it blessing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p217/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: الزكاة (11) العمل الصالح. وقال الضحاك وابن جريج: العمل الصالح الزكي.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p217/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p217/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p217/r3.claim: Being pious means Yahya was purified and committed no sin; he honored and obeyed his parents and was neither domineering nor rebellious.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p217/r3.anchor: {وكان تقيا} طهر، فلم يعمل بذنب. وقوله: {وبرا بوالديه ولم يكن جبارا عصيا}

TUSTARI:19:13/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:19:13/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:19:13/r1.claim: Hanan is mercy bestowed upon John’s parents.
TUSTARI:19:13/r1.anchor: أي فعلنا ذلك رحمة من لدنا بأبويه،

TUSTARI:19:13/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:19:13/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:19:13/r2.claim: Zakat means God purified John from people’s suspicions about him.
TUSTARI:19:13/r2.anchor: أي طهرناه من ظنون الخلق إليه فيه،

TUSTARI:19:13/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:19:13/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:19:13/r3.claim: John’s taqwa means turning toward God and away from all else; the states of prophets are wholly pure.
TUSTARI:19:13/r3.anchor: أي مقبلا علينا، معرضا عما سوانا. وقال: إن أحوال الأنبياء كلها محضة.

JISHUMI:v6p4528/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r1.claim: Ḥanān means mercy, as in the cited poetic examples of asking for mercy and tenderness.
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r1.anchor: الحنان: الرحمة، ومنه: وحنانيك أي رحمة بعد رحمة، قال الشاعر: أبا منذر أفنيت فاستبق بعضنا ... حنانيك بعض الشر أهون من بعض

JISHUMI:v6p4528/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r2.speaker: الحطيئة
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r2.claim: Al-Ḥuṭayʾa uses taḥannanī to ask ʿUmar for compassion.
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r2.anchor: وقال الحطيئة لعمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه: تحنن علي هداك المليك ... فإن لكل مقام مقالا

JISHUMI:v6p4528/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r4.claim: Ḥanānan may be coordinated with the gift of judgment, or mean that the Book was given with tenderness from God.
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r4.anchor: حنانا) قيل: نصب لأنه معطوف على الحكم، وتقديره: آتيناه حنانا

JISHUMI:v6p4528/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r5.claim: Zakāt is coordinated with ḥanān, while taqiyyan is the predicate of kāna.
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r5.anchor:
وزكاة عطف على (حنانا).
تقيا خبر (كان) أي: كان يحيى كان تقيا

JISHUMI:v6p4528/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r11.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة، الحسن
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r11.claim: They interpret ḥanān as mercy from God.
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r11.anchor: وحنانا من لدنا قيل: رحمة من عندنا، عن ابن عباس، وقتادة، والحسن

JISHUMI:v6p4528/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r12.speaker: الضحاك
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak says it is a mercy that only God can give.
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r12.anchor: وقيل: رحمة منا لا يقدر على إعطائها غيرنا، عن الضحاك

JISHUMI:v6p4528/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r15.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r15.claim: Abu Ali says God made Yahya tender-hearted toward people so he would call them to obedience.
JISHUMI:v6p4528/r15.anchor: وقيل: تحننا على العباد ورقة قلب عليهم؛ ليدعوهم إلى طاعة الله، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v6p4530/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r1.speaker: قتادة، الضحاك، ابن جريج
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r1.claim: They interpret zakāt as righteous, pure action.
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r1.anchor: قيل: لم أضاف (زكاة) إلى نفسه وهو يصير زكيا

JISHUMI:v6p4530/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r2.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r2.claim: Al-Hasan understands zakāt as Yahya's purification of those who accepted him.

JISHUMI:v6p4530/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r3.claim: Other explanations take zakāt as praise, obedience and sincerity, a gift bestowed on his parents, blessing and growth, or purification from sins through divine لطف.

JISHUMI:v6p4530/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r4.claim: Zakāt is attributed to God because Yahya's purity resulted from God's guidance and لطف, especially in childhood; alternatively he accepted the guidance when it came.
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r4.anchor: لأنه يحصل ذلك بألطافه وهدايته خصوصا في تلك الحالة من الصغر

JISHUMI:v6p4530/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r5.claim: Taqiyyan means sincere, obedient, and avoiding sins.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10/r1.claim: Ḥanānan means mercy toward his parents and others, expressed as tenderness and compassion.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10/r2.speaker: سيبويه
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10/r2.claim: Sibawayh cites a poem in which Hanan is addressed as someone asked what brought him there and whether he knows the people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10/r2.anchor: وقالت حنان ما أتى بك ههنا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10/r3.claim: An alternative construes ḥanānan as God's compassion toward Yahya; ḥanna first means longing, then came to mean tender concern and pity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10/r3.anchor: وقيل : حنانا من الله عليه . وحن : في معنى ارتاح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10/r4.claim: Calling God Ḥannān is metaphorical, just as calling Him Raḥīm is.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10/r4.anchor: وقيل لله ( حنان ) كما قيل : ( رحيم ) على سبيل الاستعارة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10/r5.claim: Zakāh is interpreted either as purity or as almsgiving, describing Yahya's kindness and charity toward people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10/r5.anchor: والزكاة : الطهارة ، وقيل الصدقة ، أي : يتعطف

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r12.claim: Ḥanānan means mercy from God; a poet's ḥanānik also means mercy and kindness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r12.anchor: أحدها : رحمة من عندنا , قاله ابن عباس وقتادة , ومنه قول الشاعر :

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r13.claim: A poet's use of ḥanānik means mercy and kindness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r13.anchor: أبا منذر أفنيت فاستبق بعضنا … حنانيك بعض الشر أهون من بعض

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r14.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r14.claim: Ḥanānan can mean tenderness or affection.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r17.claim: Ḥanānan can mean honoring or reverence.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r17.anchor: الخامس : تعظيما . السادس : يعني آتينا تحننا على العباد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r18.claim: Ḥanānan can describe giving Yaḥyā tenderness toward God's servants.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r18.anchor: الخامس : تعظيما . السادس : يعني آتينا تحننا على العباد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r19.claim: It may mean gentleness that softens hearts and hastens their response.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r19.anchor: ويحتمل سابعا : أن يكون معناه رفقا ليستعطف به القلوب وتسرع إليه الإجابة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r20.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r20.claim: Zakāh here can mean righteous, purifying deeds.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r20.anchor: أحدها : أنها العمل الصالح الزاكي , قاله ابن جريج .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r21.claim: Zakāh can mean that God praised Yaḥyā as witnesses commend a person.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r21.anchor: الثاني : زكيناه بحسن الثناء كما يزكي الشهود إنسانا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r22.speaker: ابن قتيبة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r22.claim: Zakāh can mean a charitable gift granted through Yaḥyā to his parents.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r22.anchor: الثالث : يعني صدقة به على والديه , قاله ابن قتيبة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r23.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r23.claim: Being God-fearing can mean obedience to God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r24.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p359#2/r24.claim: Being God-fearing can mean dutifulness toward his parents.

FARRA:v2p162/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p162/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p162/r4.claim: Ḥanān means mercy and is accusative to mean that God did this as mercy for his parents; zakāt means righteousness or purification for them.
FARRA:v2p162/r4.anchor: وقوله وحنانا من لدنا [13] الحنان: الرحمة (ونصب حنانا أي) وفعلنا ذلك رحمة لأبويه

MUQATIL:19:13-15/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:13-15/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:13-15/r1.claim: Hanan means mercy from God; zakāh means that God made Yahya righteous and purified him of sins, and taqī means Muslim.
MUQATIL:19:13-15/r1.anchor: يقول: رحمة من عندنا، { وزكاة } ، يعني جعله صالحا وطهره من الذنوب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#5/r1.claim: Ḥanān means compassion and mercy toward his parents and others, and is coordinated with الحكم.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#5/r1.anchor: شفقة ورحمة لابويه وغيرهما عطفا عى الحكم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#5/r2.claim: From Our presence means from God; zakāh means purity and righteousness, and Yahya did not deliberately commit sin.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#5/r2.anchor: ﴿ من لدنا ﴾ من عندنا ﴿ وزكاة ﴾ طهارة وصلاحا فلم يعمد بذنب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#5/r3.claim: He was devout, Muslim, and obedient.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#5/r3.anchor: ﴿ وزكاة ﴾ طهارة وصلاحا فلم يعمد بذنب ﴿ وكان تقيا ﴾ مسلما مطيعا

MAJAZ:v2p2#2/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p2#2/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p2#2/r4.claim: حنانا means mercy from Us; lines by Imruʾ al-Qays and al-Ḥuṭayʾa use it to mean showing mercy.
MAJAZ:v2p2#2/r4.anchor: «وحنانا من لدنا» (13) أي رحمة من عندنا، قال امرؤ القيس ابن حجر الكندى

MAJAZ:v2p2#2/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p2#2/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p2#2/r5.claim: حنانيك is a conventional dual-form expression, as Ṭarafa’s حنانيك بعض الشر shows.
MAJAZ:v2p2#2/r5.anchor: وعامة ما يستعمل فى المنطق على لفظ الاثنين، قال طرفة العبدى: أبا منذر أفنيت فاستبق بعضنا ... حنانيك بعض الشر أهون من بعض

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet says every child of Adam comes on Judgment Day with a sin except Yahya ibn Zakariyya; Qurtubi gives no grading here.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r1.anchor: كل بني آدم يأتي يوم القيامة وله ذنب

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r2.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r2.claim: Qatada says Yahya never committed or even contemplated a sin, great or small, and never desired a woman.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r2.anchor: إن يحيى عليه السلام لم يعص الله تعالى قط بصغيرة ولا كبيرة ولا هم بامرأة

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r3.claim: Mujahid says Yahya ate grass and had permanent channels for tears in his cheeks.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r3.anchor: وكان طعام يحيى عليه السلام العشب، وكان للدمع في خديه مجار ثابتة

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r4.claim: Qurtubi refers back to his discussion of Yahya as master and chaste in the account of Zakariyya.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r4.anchor:
وقد مضى الكلام في معنى قوله:
وسيدا وحصورا

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r5.claim: Hannan is grammatically coordinated with judgment.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r5.anchor: «حنانا» عطف على «الحكم». وروي عن ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says he does not know what hannan means.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r6.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: والله ما أدري ما «الحنان»؟

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r7.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r7.claim: Most commentators understand hannan as compassion, mercy, and love, an act of the inner self.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r7.anchor: الحنان الشفقة والرحمة والمحبة وهو فعل من أفعال النفس

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r8.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r8.claim: Al-Nahhas transmits two Ibn Abbas explanations: God’s compassionate mercy toward Yahya, or the mercy Yahya was given toward people to rescue them from unbelief and idolatry.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r8.anchor: أحدهما: قال: تعطف الله عز وجل عليه بالرحمة. والقول الآخر ما أعطيه من رحمة الناس حتى يخلصهم من الكفر والشرك

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r9.claim: The word derives from a she-camel’s yearning over its young; hananak and hananayk are either synonymous forms or a dual form.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r9.anchor: وأصله من حنين الناقة على ولدها. ويقال: حنانك وحنانيك قيل: هما لغتان

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r10.claim: Abu Ubayda says Arabs use hananak or hananayk, O Lord, to mean Your mercy, as in the cited Imru al-Qays poem.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r10.anchor: والعرب تقول: حنانك يا رب وحنانيك يا رب بمعنى واحد تريد رحمتك

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes hannan as mercy, tenderness, and compassion for Yahya’s parents and others.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r12.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r12.claim: Ibn al-A‘rabi distinguishes divine Hannan with a doubled n, meaning Merciful, from hannan with a light n, meaning tenderness and mercy; he also records provision and blessing as senses.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r12.anchor: الحنان من صفة الله تعالى مشددا الرحيم. والحنان مخفف: العطف والرحمة

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r13.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r13.claim: Ibn Atiyya records hannan as something sacred or exalted in God, citing Zayd ibn Amr’s vow to make Bilal’s grave a place of devotion; al-Harawi and al-Azhari gloss the story as compassion for him.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r13.anchor: والحنان في كلام العرب أيضا ما عظم من الأمور في ذات الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r14.claim: Qurtubi concludes that hannan means tenderness, in agreement with Mujahid, whether the tenderness is from God toward Yahya or from Yahya toward creation.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r14.anchor: فالحنان العطف، وكذا قال مجاهد. و«حنانا» أي تعطفا منا عليه أو منه على الخلق

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r1.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r1.claim: Ikrima interprets hannan as love; the cited poetic usage also describes spouses’ affection.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r1.anchor: عكرمة: محبة. وحنة الرجل امرأته لتوادهما

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r2.claim: Zakat here means purification, blessing, and growth in good works, making Yahya a blessing who guides people.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r2.anchor: الزكاة» التطهير والبركة والتنمية في وجوه الخير والبر

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba offers the alternative that Yahya was a charitable gift to his parents.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r3.anchor: زكاة» صدقة به على أبويه قاله ابن قتيبة

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r4.claim: Yahya was obedient to God and therefore neither committed a sin nor inclined toward one.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r4.anchor: أي مطيعا لله تعالى، ولهذا لم يعمل خطيئة ولم يلم بها

RAZI-FULL:v21p163#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p163#2/r4.speaker: الخليل
RAZI-FULL:v21p163#2/r4.claim: Ḥanān derives from yearning and distress at separation, like a camel's cry for its young; the Prophet's former palm trunk also moaned when he moved to the pulpit.
RAZI-FULL:v21p163#2/r4.anchor: أصله من الحنين وهو الارتياح والجزع للفراق

RAZI-FULL:v21p163#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p163#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v21p163#2/r5.claim: Some permit calling God al-Ḥannān in the sense of the compassionate and merciful.
RAZI-FULL:v21p163#2/r5.anchor: فأجازه بعضهم ، وجعله بمعنى الرؤوف الرحيم

RAZI-FULL:v21p163#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p163#2/r6.speaker: منهم
RAZI-FULL:v21p163#2/r6.claim: Others disallow the divine name because of the word's original associations and because no reliable report establishes it among God's names.
RAZI-FULL:v21p163#2/r6.anchor: لم يصح الخبر بهذه اللفظة في أسماء الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v21p163#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p163#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p163#2/r7.claim: If ḥanān describes God, one reading says He gave Yaḥyā judgment and mercy toward him, with zakāh as purification and honor.
RAZI-FULL:v21p163#2/r7.anchor: إنما آتيناه الحكم صبيا حنانا من لدنا عليه

RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r1.claim: If divine ḥanān is for Zakariyyā, God says He answered his prayer by giving him a son and then granted that son judgment and mercy, purifying Zakariyyā from being a rejected supplicant.
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r1.anchor: أن يكون الحنان من الله تعالى لزكريا عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r2.claim: If divine ḥanān is for Yaḥyā's community, God bestowed judgment and mercy on him for his people's benefit through his guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r2.anchor: منا على أمته لعظيم انتفاعهم بهدايته وإرشاده

RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r3.claim: If ḥanān describes Yaḥyā, it means tenderness toward people coupled with purity from neglecting obligations, since kindness can otherwise lead one to excuse wrongdoing.
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r3.anchor: آتيناه التعطف على الخلق والطهارة عن المعاصي

RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r4.claim: The account also allows that Yaḥyā never sinned or even intended sin; Qur'anic commands to show gentleness and severity together illustrate why purity must constrain mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r4.anchor: إنما جعلنا له التعطف على عباد الله مع الطهارة عن الإخلال بالواجبات

RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r5.speaker: عطاء بن رباح
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r5.claim: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Rabāḥ interprets ḥanān as honor: Waraqa tells those torturing Bilāl that if they kill him he will honor him, as a parallel use.
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r5.anchor: وفي الآية وجه آخر وهو المنقول عن عطاء بن رباح

RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك وابن جريج
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r6.claim: They interpret zakāh as a righteous, pure deed.
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك وابن جريج

RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r7.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Yaḥyā's zakāh made those who accepted him pure as well.
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r7.anchor: زكاة لمن قبل منه حتى يكونوا أزكياء عن الحسن

RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r8.claim: Another interpretation says God purified Yaḥyā by praise, as witnesses' testimony purifies a person.
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r8.anchor: زكيناه بحسن الثناء كما تزكى الشهود الإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r9.speaker: الكبي
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r9.claim: Al-Kalbī says Yaḥyā was a charitable gift that God bestowed on his parents.
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r9.anchor: صدقة تصدق الله بها على أبويه عن الكبي

RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r10.claim: Zakāh may also mean blessing and growth.

RAZI-FULL:v21p164#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p164#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p164#2/r1.claim: Calling Yaḥyā's purity a gift from God supports the view that God creates human acts; explaining it as mere enabling grace departs from the apparent wording.
RAZI-FULL:v21p164#2/r1.anchor: واعلم أن هذا يدل على أن فعل العبد خلق لله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v21p164#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p164#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p164#2/r2.claim: Pious means both avoiding what God forbids and not neglecting what He commands; it is the highest praise and describes Yaḥyā, who neither sinned nor intended sin.
RAZI-FULL:v21p164#2/r2.anchor: يتقي نهي الله فيجتنبه ويتقي أمره فلا يهمله

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r48.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r48.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r48.claim: Ḥanān connotes gentle mercy or compassion, and its being from God’s Presence marks it as divinely bestowed.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r48.anchor: a quality of mercy that can only be bestowed by God (Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r49.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r49.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r49.claim: Tenderness may mean God’s love for John or John himself as a tender mercy to Zachariah.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r49.anchor: Some suggest that a tenderness from Our Presence refers to the love and compassion God had for John (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r50.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r50.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r50.claim: Purity refers both to freedom from sin and to righteous action.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r50.anchor: John’s purity from sin as well as to his righteousness in deed (Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r51.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r51.speaker: author

NAHHAS:v3p7/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p7/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v3p7/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives one sense of حنانا as God's compassion toward John.
NAHHAS:v3p7/r13.anchor: وفي معناه قولان عن ابن عباس أحدهما قال تعطف الله جل وعز عليه

NAHHAS:v3p7/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p7/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v3p7/r14.claim: Another interpretation is mercy bestowed on John so he could save people from unbelief and evil.
NAHHAS:v3p7/r14.anchor: والقول الآخر ما أعطيه من رحمة الناس حتى يخلصهم من الكفر

NAHHAS:v3p7/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p7/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p7/r15.claim: زكاة may mean increased goodness and growth, or that God declared John pure and pious.
NAHHAS:v3p7/r15.anchor: ( وزكاة ) في معناه قولان أحدهما أنه أعطي الزيادة في الخير

TAB-FULL:v15p476/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r1.claim: He glosses ḥanān as mercy from God.
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وحنانا من لدنا} [مريم: 13] يقول: ورحمة من عندنا

TAB-FULL:v15p476/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة، في هذه الآية {وحنانا من لدنا} [مريم: 13] قال: رحمة

TAB-FULL:v15p476/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r3.claim: He glosses ḥanān as mercy from God.
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {وحنانا من لدنا} [مريم: 13] قال: رحمة من عندنا

TAB-FULL:v15p476/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r4.claim: He says this mercy is God's gift, which no one else can bestow.
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك، قوله: {وحنانا من لدنا} [مريم: 13] قال: رحمة من عندنا لا يملك عطاءها أحد غيرنا

TAB-FULL:v15p476/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r5.claim: One report takes the mercy as God's favor toward Zakariyyā, giving him the child and acting for him.
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وحنانا من لدنا} [مريم: 13] يقول: رحمة من عندنا

TAB-FULL:v15p476/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r6.claim: He glosses ḥanān as tenderness from the Lord toward Yaḥyā.
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {وحنانا من لدنا} [مريم: 13] قال: تعطفا من ربه عليه

TAB-FULL:v15p476/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r7.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r7.claim: He glosses ḥanān as love toward Yaḥyā.
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة، {وحنانا من لدنا} [مريم: 13] قال: محبة عليه

TAB-FULL:v15p476/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p476/r8.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وحنانا} [مريم: 13] قال: أما الحنان فالمحبة

TAB-FULL:v15p477/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r1.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r1.claim: He interprets ḥanān as exaltation or honoring from God.
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r1.anchor: عن عطاء بن أبي رباح، {وحنانا من لدنا} [مريم: 13] قال: تعظيما من لدنا

TAB-FULL:v15p477/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r2.claim: He says he does not know what ḥanān means.
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r2.anchor: أنه قال: لا أدري ما الحنان

TAB-FULL:v15p477/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r3.claim: Arabic uses ḥanānaka and ḥanānik; grammarians differ whether the latter is a dual form or a dialectal expression, and cited poems illustrate the forms.
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r3.anchor: وللعرب في حنانك لغتان: حنانك يا ربنا، وحنانيك

TAB-FULL:v15p477/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r4.speaker: طرفة بن العبد
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r4.claim: His poem uses ḥanānik as an example of the form.
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r4.anchor: أبا منذر أفنيت فاستبق بعضنا … حنانيك بعض الشر أهون من بعض

TAB-FULL:v15p477/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r5.speaker: امرؤ القيس
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r5.claim: His poem illustrates the other form, ḥanānaka.
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r5.anchor: ويمنحها بنو شمجى بن جرم … معيزهم حنانك ذا الحنان

TAB-FULL:v15p477/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r6.claim: The root denotes longing or inclination; taḥannana means tenderness, compassion, and mercy, and ḥanān is its verbal noun.
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r6.anchor: وأصل ذلك أعني الحنان، من قول القائل: حن فلان إلى كذا وذلك إذا ارتاح إليه

TAB-FULL:v15p477/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r7.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r7.claim: A poem uses taḥannan ʿalayya to mean showing tenderness and compassion.
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r7.anchor: تحنن علي هداك المليك … فإن لكل مقام مقالا

TAB-FULL:v15p477/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r8.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r8.claim: A rajaz line calls a wife ḥannah, reflecting the husband's tenderness and affection.
TAB-FULL:v15p477/r8.anchor: وليلة ذات دجى سريت … ولم تضرني حنة وبيت

TAB-FULL:v15p480/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p480/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p480/r1.claim: Zakāh is purification from sins and using the body in God's obedience; it coordinates grammatically with wisdom.
TAB-FULL:v15p480/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قوله: {وزكاة} [مريم: 13] قال: العمل الصالح الزكي

TAB-FULL:v15p480/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p480/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p480/r2.claim: He glosses zakāh as good action.
TAB-FULL:v15p480/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وزكاة} [مريم: 13] قال: الزكاة: العمل الصالح

TAB-FULL:v15p480/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p480/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v15p480/r3.claim: He glosses zakāh as righteous, pure action.
TAB-FULL:v15p480/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قوله: {وزكاة} [مريم: 13] قال: العمل الصالح الزكي

TAB-FULL:v15p480/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p480/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v15p480/r4.claim: He glosses zakāh as righteous action.
TAB-FULL:v15p480/r4.anchor: قال: سمعت الضحاك، يقول: في قوله {وزكاة} [مريم: 13] يعني العمل الصالح الزاكي

TAB-FULL:v15p480#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p480#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p480#2/r1.claim: Taqiyyan means fearing God, fulfilling duties, avoiding prohibitions, and hastening to obey Him.
TAB-FULL:v15p480#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {وزكاة وكان تقيا} [مريم: 13] قال: طهر فلم يعمل بذنب

TAB-FULL:v15p480#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p480#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p480#2/r2.claim: He says Yaḥyā was purified and committed no sin.
TAB-FULL:v15p480#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {وزكاة وكان تقيا} [مريم: 13] قال: طهر فلم يعمل بذنب

TAB-FULL:v15p480#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p480#2/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p480#2/r3.claim: He remarks that people already know the meanings of zakāh and piety.
TAB-FULL:v15p480#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وزكاة وكان تقيا} [مريم: 13] قال: أما الزكاة والتقوى فقد عرفهما الناس

TABATABAI:19:12-13/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:12-13/r4.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:19:12-13/r4.claim: Hanan means tenderness and compassion and is associated with mercy.
TABATABAI:19:12-13/r4.anchor: ولكون الإشفاق لا ينفك من الرحمة عبر عن الرحمة بالحنان

TABATABAI:19:12-13/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:12-13/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:19:12-13/r5.claim: Hanan is interpreted as mercy, perhaps prophethood or divine friendship, or as love from people, compassion toward them, or God’s special tenderness toward Yahya.
TABATABAI:19:12-13/r5.anchor: وفسر الحنان في الآية بالرحمة ولعل المراد بها النبوة أو الولاية

TABATABAI:19:12-13/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:12-13/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:12-13/r6.claim: Because hanan is from God and lies outside ordinary causes, the context favors a special divine attraction and bond between Yahya and his Lord, setting aside readings as popular affection or his own compassion for people.
TABATABAI:19:12-13/r6.anchor: أن المراد به نوع عطف وانجذاب خاص إلهي بينه وبين ربه غير مألوف

TABATABAI:19:12-13/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:12-13/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:12-13/r7.claim: Zakat fundamentally means sound growth; it may describe God’s care nurturing Yahya or Yahya’s own love and attraction toward God, with growth of the spirit.

TABATABAI:19:13-15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:13-15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:13-15/r1.claim: Zakat is not best read as blessing, charity, or purity from sins; its basic sense of beneficial growth fits the surrounding description better.
TABATABAI:19:13-15/r1.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر وهن ما قيل إن المراد بالزكاة البركة

TABATABAI:19:15/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:15/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:19:15/r5.claim: Al-Baqir explains “compassion from Us” as God's tenderness toward John; when John called “My Lord,” God answered, “Here I am, John.”
TABATABAI:19:15/r5.anchor: تحنن الله. قلت فما بلغ من تحنن الله عليه

TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r3.claim: The Qur'an praises John as affirming Jesus's prophethood, a leader, chaste, prophet, righteous, elect and guided; God named him uniquely, gave him wisdom as a child, and greeted him at the three stages.
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r3.anchor: كان مصدقا بكلمة من الله وهو تصديقه بنبوة المسيح

TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r4.claim: John was born miraculously to an elderly father and barren mother, embraced worship and asceticism from childhood, never married, and lived alongside Jesus whom he affirmed.
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r4.anchor: فقد كان أبوه شيخا فانيا وأمه عاقرا

TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r5.claim: John was loved by his people and gathered them to preach repentance and piety until he was martyred.
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r5.anchor: تحن إليه القلوب وتميل إليه النفوس ويجتمع إليه الناس فيعظهم

TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r6.claim: One report says a woman beloved by the Israelite king sought John's head after he rebuked the king's conduct; the king ordered John beheaded and his head given to her.
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r6.anchor: امرأة بغيا افتتن بها ملك بني إسرائيل وكان يأتيها فنهاه يحيى

TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r7.claim: Another report says the king's niece asked for John's head after her mother prompted her when the king sought to marry her, because John had forbidden the marriage.
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r7.anchor: ابنة أخي الملك وكان يريد أن يتزوج بها فنهاه يحيى

TABRISI:19:12-13/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:12-13/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:12-13/r1.claim: Hanan fundamentally means mercy or tenderness; the commentary illustrates it with lines from Imru al-Qays, another poet, Tarafa, and al-Hutayia.
TABRISI:19:12-13/r1.anchor: أصل الحنان الرحمة يقال حنانك وحنانيك

TABRISI:19:13-15/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:13-15/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:19:13-15/r1.claim: Zakah can mean obedience to God and sincerity.
TABRISI:19:13-15/r1.anchor: يعني بالزكاة طاعة الله والإخلاص عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:19:13-15/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:13-15/r2.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:19:13-15/r2.claim: Zakah may be a gift of charity from God to Yahya’s parents.
TABRISI:19:13-15/r2.anchor: وقيل: معناه وصدقة تصدق الله به على أبويه عن الكلبي.

TABRISI:19:13-15/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:13-15/r3.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:19:13-15/r3.claim: Another view says God purified Yahya with good praise, as witnesses purify a person by their testimony.
TABRISI:19:13-15/r3.anchor: وقيل: معناه وزكيناه بحسن الثناء عليه كما يزكي الشهود الإنسان عن الجبائي.

TABRISI:19:13-15/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:13-15/r4.speaker: قالوا
TABRISI:19:13-15/r4.claim: Yahya was so pious that he neither committed nor intended a sin.
TABRISI:19:13-15/r4.anchor: وكان من تقواه أنه لم يعمل خطيئة ولم يهم بها

TABRISI:19:13-15/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:13-15/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:13-15/r5.claim: Asiyya is an active participle meaning disobedient to his Lord.
TABRISI:19:13-15/r5.anchor: { عصيا } أي عاصيا لربه فعيل بمعنى فاعل.

TABRISI:19:13-15/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:13-15/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:19:13-15/r6.claim: Jabbar may mean someone who kills or strikes in anger.
TABRISI:19:13-15/r6.anchor: وقيل: الجبار الذي يقتل ويضرب على الغضب عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:19:13-15/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:13-15/r7.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:19:13-15/r7.claim: Peace can mean safety and protection from God; Yahya is protected from Satan at birth, worldly trials and grave punishment at death, and the terror of resurrection and Hell.
TABRISI:19:13-15/r7.anchor: وقيل: وسلامة وأمان له منا عن الكلبي ومعناه سلامة وأمن له يوم ولد من عبث الشيطان به

TABRISI:19:13-15/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:13-15/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:13-15/r8.claim: God attributes Yahya’s purity to Himself because divine لطف guided him, especially in childhood, and enabled his obedience.
TABRISI:19:13-15/r8.anchor: أنه إنما صار كذلك بإلطاف من الله لا سيما في تلك الحالة

THALABI:v6p207#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p207#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p207#2/r3.claim: Ḥanān means mercy or compassion, supported by lines from al-Hutayʾa and Tarafa; the word derives from a mother's longing for her calf.
THALABI:v6p207#2/r3.anchor: وحنانا من لدنا رحمة من عندنا، قال الحطيئة لعمر بن الخطاب:

THALABI:v6p207#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p207#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p207#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says he does not know hanān except as God's tender mercy toward His servants.
THALABI:v6p207#2/r4.anchor: قال: ما أدري ما حنانا إلا أن يكون بعطف رحمة الله عز وجل على عباده

THALABI:v6p207#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p207#2/r5.speaker: عوف
THALABI:v6p207#2/r5.claim: Awf says he heard hanān explained as love.
THALABI:v6p207#2/r5.anchor: عن عوف بلغني في قوله الله عز وجل وحنانا من لدنا قال: الحنان: المحبة

THALABI:v6p207#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p207#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p207#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses zakāh as obedience to God and sincerity.
THALABI:v6p207#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس يعني بالزكاة طاعة الله عز وجل والإخلاص.

THALABI:v6p207#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p207#2/r7.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v6p207#2/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak says zakāh is righteous, pure action.
THALABI:v6p207#2/r7.anchor: وقال الضحاك: هي الفعل الزاكي الصالح،

THALABI:v6p207#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p207#2/r8.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v6p207#2/r8.claim: Al-Kalbi says zakāh means charity Yahya's father gave to his parents.
THALABI:v6p207#2/r8.anchor: وقال الكلبي: يعني صدقة تصدق والده بها على أبويه،

THALABI:v6p207#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p207#2/r9.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v6p207#2/r9.claim: Other glosses take zakāh as blessing and increase, or as God's making Yahya pure from sins.
THALABI:v6p207#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: بركة ونماء وزيادة. وقيل: جعلناه طاهرا من الذنوب.

THALABI:v6p207#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p207#2/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p207#2/r10.claim: Yahya was a Muslim, sincere, and obedient servant.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r1.claim: Hanan in Arabic denotes tenderness, compassion, and mercy; the cited verse of poetry witnesses the word's use.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r1.anchor: الحنان معناه في اللغة: العطف والرحمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، رواية علي بن أبي طلحة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r2.claim: He explains God's hanan as mercy from Him, as do Ikrima, Qatada, and al-Rabiʿ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r2.anchor: ابن عباس في رواية علي بن أبي طلحة: {وحنانا من لدنا} يقول:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r3.claim: Zakah means obedience to God and sincerity.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r4.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r4.claim: Zakah means righteous deeds; al-Dahhak and Ibn Jurayj share this interpretation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r4.anchor: قتادة: (هي العمل الصالح) (¬4). وهو قول الضحاك وابن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r5.claim: On this reading Yahya is described: God gave him mercy and tenderness toward people, so he would call them to obedience, and gave him sincere good works.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r5.anchor: في إخلاص، فعلى هذا الموصوف بالحنان والزكاة يحيى؛ لأن الله آتاه إياهما.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، رواية عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r6.claim: He says he does not know the meaning of hanan, but thinks it is God's affection for His servant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r6.anchor: ابن عباس في رواية عكرمة: (لا أدري ما الحنان؟ غير أني أظنه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r7.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r7.claim: He likewise takes hanan as tenderness from the Lord toward Yahya.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r8.claim: He explains zakah as purification; on this view God is the subject who shows tenderness to and purifies Yahya.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r9.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r9.claim: Another view refers hanan and zakah to Zechariah; al-Farra says the child's gift was mercy to the parents.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r9.anchor: وقال قوم: الحنان والزكاة يعودان إلى زكريا، وهو قول الكلبي والفراء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r10.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r10.claim: This interpretation requires an ellipsis: the child and answered prayer were mercy and a charitable gift to Zechariah.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p207/r10.anchor: وفعلنا ذلك يعني هبة الولد واستجابة الدعاء حنانا من لدنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p209/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p209/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p209/r1.claim: Yahya feared God and did not associate anyone with Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p209/r1.anchor: جعلته يتقيني ولا يعدل بي غيري

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p209/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p209/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p209/r2.claim: They say Yahya committed no sin and did not even intend one; a prophetic report exempts him from the ordinary case of people who intend or commit sin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p209/r2.anchor: وكان من تقواه أنه لم يعمل خطيئة ولا هم بها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:11-16/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:11-16/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:11-16/r3.claim: God gave Yahya compassion, meaning mercy, and zakat, meaning purification.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:11-16/r3.anchor: وحنانا } وآتيناه حنانا: رحمة { من لدنا وزكاة } تطهيرا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p216/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p216/r10.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p216/r10.claim: Ḥanānan min ladunnā means tenderness bestowed from God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p216/r10.anchor: قوله: {وحنانا من لدنا} [مريم: 13] أي: من عندنا، أي: وأعطيناه حنانا من لدنا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p216/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p216/r11.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p216/r11.claim: Mujāhid interprets ḥanān as his Lord's tenderness toward him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p216/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد: تعطفا من ربه عليه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p216/r12.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p216/r12.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والكلبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p216/r12.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and al-Kalbī explain ḥanān as mercy from God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p216/r12.anchor:
وقال الحسن وقتادة: أي: رحمة من عندنا.
وقال الكلبي: الحنان، الرحمة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p217/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p217/r1.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p217/r1.claim: Qatāda says zakāt means righteous action.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p217/r1.anchor: قوله: {وزكاة} [مريم: 13] سعيد، عن قتادة قال: الزكاة العمل الصالح.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p217/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p217/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p217/r2.claim: Yaḥyā says Qatāda derived this meaning from the verse about believers who perform good works receiving the highest ranks, which is the reward of the purified.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p217/r2.anchor: قال يحيى: رويت أنه أخذه من هذه الآية في { [طه:] ومن يأته مؤمنا قد عمل الصالحات فأولئك لهم الدرجات العلى

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p217/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p217/r3.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p217/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Yahya's zakāt makes those who accept him purified.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p217/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: زكاة لمن قبل عنه حتى يكونوا أزكياء.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p217/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p217/r5.speaker: النبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p217/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports the Prophet saying that no human has committed or intended a sin except Yahya ibn Zakariyya.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p217/r5.anchor: المبارك بن فضالة والربيع بن صبيح عن الحسن قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ما من آدمي»

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:13/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:13/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:13/r1.claim: God created Yahya with pure nature: he was compassionate, reverent, devoted, dutiful to parents, attentive to people's rights, and free of tyranny and disobedience.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:13/r1.anchor: O, insanlara karşı son derecede şefkatli, Allah’a karşı saygılı, dinine bağlı, ana-babasına iyilik eden

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:13/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:13/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:13/r2.claim: Another verse describes Yahya as affirming God's scripture, chaste, noble, and a righteous prophet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:13/r2.anchor: onun, Allah’ın kitabını tasdik eden, iffetli, asil ve sâlih bir peygamber olduğu ifade buyurulmuştur

SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r1.claim: Hanan may be a direct object coordinated with the earlier object, meaning God gave John tenderness.
SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مفعولا به نسقا على

SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda cites taḥannan and says hanan is more commonly used in the dual, as in ḥanānik.
SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r3.anchor:
وأنشد أبو / عبيدة:
3215- تحنن علي هداك المليك
فإن لكل مقام مقالا
قال: " وأكثر استعماله مثنى

SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows hanan as a supplicatory verbal noun, like suqyan or raʿyan, governed by an omitted verb.
SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r4.anchor: وجوز فيه أبو البقاء أن يكون مصدرا

SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r5.claim: Hanan may instead be nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, like the cited expression in Yusuf.
SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يرتفع على خبر ابتداء مضمر

SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r6.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r6.claim: Sibawayh's poem uses ḥanān as a nominative expression, supporting that construction.
SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r6.anchor:
وأنشد سيبويه:
3217- وقالت حنان ما أتى بك ههنا

SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says calling God Ḥanān, as one calls Him Merciful, is metaphorical.
SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r7.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " وذلك على سبيل الاستعارة ".

SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:13/r8.claim: The phrase min ladunna qualifies hanan.

ZAJJAJ:v3p321/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p321/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p321/r8.claim: Ḥanānan means tenderness, affection, and mercy; zakāh means purification.

ZAJJAJ:v3p321/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p321/r9.speaker: قال الشاعر
ZAJJAJ:v3p321/r9.claim: An unidentified poem uses ḥanān to mean affection or mercy; the witnessed word is ḥanān.
ZAJJAJ:v3p321/r9.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
فقالت حنان ما أتى بك ههنا. . . أذو نسب

ZAJJAJ:v3p321/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p321/r10.speaker: قال أيضا
ZAJJAJ:v3p321/r10.claim: Another poem uses ḥanānikay in a plea for compassion; the word witnesses the sense of tenderness.
ZAJJAJ:v3p321/r10.anchor:
وقال أيضا:
أبا منذر أفنيت فاستبق بعضنا. . . حنانيك

ASAD-NOTES:19:12#n11/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:12#n11/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:12#n11/r1.claim: The compassion bestowed on John is a special gift from God.
ASAD-NOTES:19:12#n11/r1.anchor: "compassion from Us" - i.e., as a special divine gift

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The prophets in Adam’s, Noah’s, and Abraham’s lines preached monotheism, prayer, and zakāh, but their followers turned to polytheism, abandoned the rites, and followed innovations and desires.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: all celebrated prophets born in the progeny of Adam (sws), Noah (sws) and Abraham (sws) preached monotheism.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet is urged to persevere against their hostility and is given glad tidings of success.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the Prophet (sws) is urged to show perseverance on their attitude and given glad tidings of success.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The adversaries mistake worldly success for proof of their truth; it is only respite until the truth is conclusively conveyed and they have no excuse when seized.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: they regard their worldly successes in contrast to the believers to be a reason of their own veracity.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Jesus and Mary are prominent because Christians and Jews secretly supported Quraysh; the Qur’an exposes the People of the Book to show they cannot support a truthless cause.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the Christians too had begun to secretly support the Quraysh.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Zacharias story introduces Mary’s story and counters Christians who treat Jesus’s miraculous birth as proof of his divinity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This incident forms a prelude to the anecdote of Mary (sws) mentioned subsequently.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Hanan means love, liveliness, and compassion; Islahi finds it strange that some attributed to Ibn Abbas ignorance of this common Arabic word.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: means love, liveliness and compassion. This word is a very common Arabic word and it is strange how some people have ascribed this opinion to Ibn ‘Abbās

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Hanan describes a living, vibrant heart and soul rather than an inert existence; John's quality was profound, as his Gospel statements still move people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This trait signifies that the heart and soul of a person are vibrant and living.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Zakāh here means purity and cleanliness, inward and outward, and reflects the inner compassion denoted by hanan.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Obviously, this refers to both inner and outer purity. It is actually a reflection of

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Taqī points to John's devout deeds and ascetic life: he publicly called people to repent, lived simply, and gave his life for God's Book.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This word points to John’s (sws) deeds and character: he was devout and pious.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p4#7/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p4#7/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p4#7/r1.claim: Qatada glosses hanan as mercy from God.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p4#7/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وحنانا من لدنا ﴾ قال رحمة من عندنا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p4#7/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p4#7/r2.speaker: وهب
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p4#7/r2.claim: Wahb reports a heavenly herald declaring Yahya the foremost of those born to women.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p4#7/r2.anchor: سمعت وهبا يقول نادى مناد من السماء أن يحيى بن زكريا سيد من ولدت النساء

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p4#7/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p4#7/r3.speaker: وهب
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p4#7/r3.claim: The same heavenly declaration names Jirjis the foremost of the martyrs.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p4#7/r3.anchor: نادى مناد من السماء أن يحيى بن زكريا سيد من ولدت النساء وأن جرجس سيد الشهداء

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p4#7/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p4#7/r4.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p4#7/r4.claim: In a report through Shah b. Hawshab, Jesus sought rain after sending sinners away; only a man who had gouged out an eye after a forbidden look remained, and his prayer brought rain.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p4#7/r4.anchor: عن رجل عن شهر بن حوشب أن عيسى بن مريم خرج يستسقي وخرج بالناس ثم قال لهم من كان ذا ذنب فليرجع

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p5/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p5/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains hanan as God's compassion toward His servants.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p5/r1.anchor: عن رجل عن أبيه عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى ﴿ وحنانا من لدنا ﴾ قال ترحم الله على العباد

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p5/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p5/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p5/r2.anchor: أنا قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وزكاة ﴾ قال صدقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan like the previous one; Muqatil exempts the prostration verse, saying it was revealed in Medina after the migration to Abyssinia.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية كالسورة التي قبلها. وقال مقاتل: إلا آية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.claim: The surahs connect through astonishing stories: the earlier tells of the Cave, Moses and Khidr, and Dhul-Qarnayn; this one of John’s birth to an old man and barren woman and Jesus’ birth without a father.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.anchor: ومناسبتها لما قبلها أنه تعالى ضمن السورة قبلها قصصا عجبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r11.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وعكرمة وقتادة والضحاك وأبو عبيدة والفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r11.claim: They interpret ḥanān as mercy; Abū ʿUbayda cites a poem asking the king for compassion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r11.anchor: والحنان الرحمة قاله ابن عباس في رواية والحسن وعكرمة وقتادة والضحاك وأبو عبيدة والفراء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r12.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r12.claim: Abū ʿUbayda notes that ḥanān is often used in the dual, as in the cited proverb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r12.anchor: قال: وأكثر ما تستعمل مثنى كما قال: حنانيك بعض الشر أهون من بعض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r13.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r13.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says God made Yahya a source of mercy for the people of his era.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r13.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: المعنى وجعلناه حنانا لأهل زمانه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r14.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r14.claim: Mujāhid explains ḥanān as God's tenderness and compassion toward Yahya.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r14.anchor: وقال مجاهد وتعطفا من ربه عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r15.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r15.claim: Ibn Jubayr interprets ḥanān as gentleness.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r16.speaker: عكرمة وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r16.claim: ʿIkrima and Ibn Zayd interpret ḥanān as love.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r18.speaker: الضحاك وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r18.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Qatāda explain zakāh as righteous deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r18.anchor: وقوله وزكاة عن الضحاك وقتادة عملا صالحا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r19.speaker: ابن السائب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r19.claim: Ibn al-Sāʾib says the zakāh was charity given for Yahya's parents.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r19.anchor: وعن ابن السائب: صدقة تصدق بها على أبويه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r21.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r21.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī interprets zakāh as an increase in goodness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r21.anchor: وعن ابن الأنباري زيادة في الخير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r22.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r22.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p245/r22.claim: Another interpretation is praise, as when witnesses are declared upright.
